pride_data.title: Identification of a direct interaction between the Fab domains of IgG antibodies and human FcRn upon IgG-FcRn complex formation
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the interaction between IgG-type antibodies and the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn). Different cross-linking chemistries were used, including disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS); a combination of pimelic dihydrazide (PDH) in combination with the zero-length cross-linking reagent, DMTMM; and the Xplex method using hexanediamine and N-hydroxybenzotriazole.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures: Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014, for DSS; Leitner et al., PNAS, 2014, for PDH/DMTMM; and Fioramonte et al., Anal. Chem., 2018, for Xplex. Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin or with Asp-N protease. Digests (in-solution or in-gel) were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography and SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Elite instrument. Duplicate injections of three to four SEC fractions were performed. A detailed overview of all experimental conditions (protein composition of the samples, cross-linking chemistries, enzymes, etc.) is provided in the spreadsheet “File_list_FcRn.xlsx” submitted together with the experimental data. Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against the sequences of target proteins and additional proteins identified as contaminants. For Lys-C/trypsin digestion, protease specificity was set to cleavage after K and R unless followed by P; for Asp-N, D and E were defined as possible cleavage sites. In both cases, a maximum of two missed cleavages per peptide was allowed (excluding the cross-linking site, if applicable). The precursor mass error was ±15 ppm (orbitrap detection), the fragment mass error 0.2 Da and 0.3 Da for the detection of “common” and “xlink” fragment ion types (detection in the linear ion trap). The false discovery rate was adjusted to less than 0.05 at the non-redundant peptide pair level by xProphet. All cross-link identifications are compiled in tables in Microsoft Excel format that are included with the submission.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; pdh; dmtmm; xplex; structural proteomics; antibody – receptor interactions
